data.label: Synthetic device simulator
data.description: Existing test source that sends JSON events {deviceId, timestamp, value, unit}. Outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Event ingestion & buffer
data.description: Receives events and holds them durably for a retention window that is still to be agreed. Partitions by deviceId to keep per-device order. Consumers use checkpoints so processing can be replayed.

data.label: Validation function
data.description: Event Hubs-triggered function. Checks the schema, the required deviceId, timestamp and unit, and the allowed units. Passes the original fields through unchanged.

data.label: Invalid event quarantine
data.description: Private container that stores rejected events with the rejection reason, for review and replay.

data.label: Anomaly scoring endpoint
data.description: Returns an anomaly score per event. The model isn't chosen yet. Local tests use a scripted reply, which does not validate model quality.
data.service: Azure Machine Learning managed online endpoint

data.label: Anomaly results store
data.description: Stores the score with deviceId, timestamp, unit and model version. Uses deviceId as the partition key. Writes are idempotent per event ID.

data.label: Operator alerting
data.description: Raises an alert when a score is at or above the agreed threshold. The threshold and the notification channel are still to be agreed.

data.label: Operator
data.description: Person who receives and handles anomaly alerts.

decisions.subject: design.azure-sensor-anomaly-detection-first-end-to-end-sketch
decisions.title: Azure sensor anomaly detection: first end-to-end sketch
decisions.context: Scope: synthetic sensor events → Event Hubs (ingest and durable buffer) → Functions validator (schema, units; invalid events go to Blob quarantine) → Azure ML online endpoint (anomaly score) → Cosmos DB results → Azure Monitor alert → operator. Assumptions: region and subscription aren't chosen, the model isn't selected or validated, and local tests use a scripted model reply. Azure isn't covered by native Terraform here, so these components need engineering work. The diagram doesn't prove deployment or connectivity.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.

needs.statement: Every event keeps its device ID, event timestamp and measurement unit unchanged from intake through to results and alerts. Events missing any of these are rejected to quarantine with a reason.
needs.rationale: If identity or units are lost, anomaly results can't be traced or trusted, and mixed units can cause false alarms.
needs.basis: User: "Preserve device identity, timestamps and units."

needs.statement: Proposed: accepted events stay buffered durably so processing can resume or replay after a downstream failure without losing data.
needs.rationale: Without a buffer, an outage in validation or inference loses events. The retention period still needs to be agreed.

needs.statement: Proposed: the operator gets an alert for each anomaly at or above the agreed score threshold, including device ID, timestamp and score. Repeated alerts for the same device are suppressed.
needs.rationale: Too many false alarms make operators ignore alerts. The threshold and acceptable false-alarm rate are still open.
